purpose: Topotecan is a chemotherapy medicine used to treat certain types of cancer, including ovarian cancer, small cell lung cancer, and cervical cancer. It is usually given when other cancer treatments have not worked well enough. Your doctor has chosen this medicine because it can help slow or stop cancer cells from growing.
how_it_works: Cancer cells need to copy their DNA in order to grow and spread. Topotecan works by blocking a special protein called topoisomerase I, which cancer cells need to do this copying process. Without that protein working properly, the cancer cells cannot reproduce and they eventually die off.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include low blood cell counts (which can make you tired, increase your risk of infection, or cause easy bruising or bleeding), nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, hair loss, mouth sores, and feeling very fatigued or weak. Most side effects are manageable, and your care team will monitor you closely.
warnings: Because topotecan lowers your white blood cell counts, you are at higher risk for serious infections — call your doctor right away if you have a fever, chills, or signs of infection. It can also cause severe bleeding due to low platelet counts. This medicine can harm an unborn baby, so do not become pregnant or father a child while on this treatment. Let your doctor know all other medicines you take, as some can interact with topotecan.
typical_dosing: Topotecan is usually given through an IV (into your vein) once a day for 5 days in a row, repeated every 3 weeks. It can also be given as a capsule taken by mouth once a day for 5 days every 3 weeks for certain cancers. Your exact dose will be calculated based on your body size and overall health, and your doctor will adjust it as needed.
